In 2024, the child poverty rate in Alberta was **12.8%**. That is the share of people under 18 below the Market Basket Measure (MBM) poverty line, which is Canada's official poverty line. This figure uses the 2023-base MBM. It is the latest year available in the table, and Statistics Canada rates its quality "C" (good).

The rate has risen in recent years: 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022 and 11.9% in 2023.

Other low-income measures, such as the after-tax Low Income Measure, give different rates. This table also carries them, but I did not pull those figures.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, Canadian Income Survey, vector v1792632015 (Alberta, persons under 18 years, MBM 2023 base, percentage of persons in low income), reference year 2024.


In 2025, Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration paid an average of **$1,702.65 per week**, including overtime, for all employees. That is about $88,500 a year if you multiply by 52, which is my own calculation and not a published figure.

Recent years for the same series:

| Year | Average weekly earnings |
|---|---|
| 2023 | $1,703.25 |
| 2024 | $1,677.47 |
| 2025 | $1,702.65 |

- **Industry grouping:** Statistics Canada publishes this industry as "Provincial and territorial public administration". For Alberta, that means the provincial government only.
- **Excluding overtime:** A separate series (v1797937) covers earnings excluding overtime. I didn't retrieve its values.
- **Hourly wages:** I did not look for an hourly average.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415, annual, reference years 2023 to 2025.

In 2024, the average total income of individuals in Alberta was **$63,200**. This is before tax and includes government transfers. It is in 2024 constant dollars and covers persons aged 15 and over. The data-quality grade is A (excellent).

Recent years, in 2024 constant dollars:

| Year | Average total income |
|---|---|
| 2020 | $65,300 |
| 2021 | $66,000 |
| 2022 | $63,400 |
| 2023 | $63,900 |
| 2024 | $63,200 |

"Income" can mean other things. Market income (before taxes and transfers) and after-tax income are also in this table, and I didn't pull them. The median is also lower than the average, and I didn't pull that either.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0091-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v1529672282, reference year 2024.

For the national figure, 12.6% of persons with disabilities aged 15 and over were below the poverty line in 2024. That uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base) and is data quality B. The rate was 12.9% in 2022 and 12.8% in 2023. The source is Table 11-10-0090-01, vector v1793292452.

Table 11-10-0087-01 does have provincial data by disability status, but it covers income distribution, not poverty rates.
